contentBlocks.value: Result: 5/2, which matches the right-hand side

strategyBlocks.value: Divide both sides by 2 to remove the bracket's coefficient, then add 1.

whyThisWorks.value: Dividing a fraction by 2 is the same as multiplying it by 1/2, so 5/2 becomes 5/4 — the fraction gets smaller because the parts are halved. Adding 1 then requires writing 1 as 4/4 so the two fractions have the same denominator. Nothing about the method changes when fractions appear; only the arithmetic within each step does.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing 5/2 by 2 to get 5 by cancelling the 2s incorrectly.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing 5/2 by 2 to get 5 by cancelling the 2s incorrectly.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding 1 to 5/4 as 6/4 by adding 1 to the numerator only.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding 1 to 5/4 as 6/4 by adding 1 to the numerator only.

examTip.value: If fractions make you uneasy, multiply every term by the denominator at the start: 2(x − 1) = 5/2 becomes 4(x − 1) = 5. The answer is the same and the working is fraction-free until the last line.
